summary: This is a direct port of a measured 14-23% FA3 gain on the same kernel (hq=16, hkv=2, d=64, FP8 page-1 cache). The batch>1 gate drops the shapes where attention_decode lost. Because the full layer has weight 16 against the sliding layer's 46, the expected headline gain is only about +1.8%, inside the drift. So the run must be judged on the FA3 kernel row and the per-shape full-layer rows, and no companion is needed.
justification: The mechanism is plausible, and it has been measured on this exact kernel already. In FINDINGS, the full-layer FA3 kernel takes 188.8 us at decode_16, 374.4 at decode_32, 191.9 at verify_16 and 374.0 at verify_32. In attention_decode's base the same kernel took 194/378/198/383 us, so the geometry and the kernel are the same, and pairing took those to 165/307/173/309 us there (job facc479992e24a35, 16/16 tests). Every load here is 46 sliding steps plus 16 full steps. Taking the brief's savings (25-30, 60-70, 20-25 and 65-75 us per full shape) gives these load gains: decode_32 ~4.9% (about 1040 us of 21306), decode_16 ~2.3%, verify_32 ~2.5%, verify_16 ~1.2%, and 0 for decode_1/verify_1. The geomean comes to about +1.8%, which is below the ±1.5% CI resolution plus the 1.5-2.5% per-shape drift in LESSONS. The brief's per-shape expectations (faster on full B=16/32, flat on sliding and B=1) agree with the TASK weights. The brief's '~1.5-3% per load' undersells decode_32 and oversells verify_16, but the directions are right. The full-shape floors (137.5-267.2 us for the whole layer) leave ample room. In decode_layer, FA3 runs alone on the main stream between store_cache and o_norm_gate, with nothing overlapping it. Weakest link: the net per-call overhead. The brief counts zeros, two pad copies, empty and two un-pad copies, minus the removed cast, as ~1 us. Inside a captured graph each tiny elementwise node costs roughly 1.5-3 us (LESSONS: graph-node residuals of ~0.3-4 us), and dropping the judge's scheduler_metadata makes FA3 run its own prepare_varlen_num_blocks launch on decode. A realistic overhead is therefore 5-10 us per full B=16/32 call. That is still small against 25-70 us saved, but at verify_16 the per-load gain could shrink to ~0.8%. Second link: the BF16->E4M3 cast now happens in a strided copy_ into a non-contiguous destination. The values are identical (copy_ and .to share the same conversion), but these are two strided TensorIterator kernels rather than one contiguous cast, which is negligible at tokens x 16 x 64.
confounders: marlin-block-m-cap-16: no confound. It changes only the MoE Marlin GEMMs, which run after o GEMM with no stream overlap against FA3 and no shared memory traffic within the call; its effect is in the baseline equally for both sides of the A/B against best.

sglang-pipeline-parity-router-hilo-m8: no separable confound. It is the base pipeline that produces q as BF16 from FusedQKNorm and casts inline; the hypothesis already folds that cast into the pad. The router side-stream overlaps the pooler, not FA3. Reverting it would remove the whole pipeline the change is written against, so an ab-revert is meaningless.
interference: No companion is needed. If the run gains, the FA3 kernel row (cutlass flash_fwd) on the four full B=16/32 shapes drops toward ~165/307/173/309 us while sliding and B=1 stay flat, and only the paired geometry can cause that. If it loses or comes out flat, the profile splits the causes three ways without another run. First, the paired FA3 kernel is itself slower (its own row). Second, the split/combine schedule changed because the judge's metadata was dropped (the FlashAttnFwdCombine row, and the extra prepare launch on decode only). Third, pad/un-pad overhead (the new small copy rows plus the shape-minus-kernel-sum residual). A 'keep the judge metadata' control cannot be built, because that metadata was made for hdim 64 / Hkv 2. A num_splits control would duplicate the queued fa3-num-splits-full-no-metadata and fa3-full-single-split-probe. The B=1 gate is self-controlling: decode_1/verify_1 full run master's code byte for byte, so any movement there is drift and tells you the run's noise level. Harvest instruction: classify on FA3's own us and the per-shape full-layer ratios, not the headline, since about +1.8% expected can land as 'within-ci' while the mechanism is fully confirmed. Note that triton-flash-decode-full-oversub-kv-prefetch (queued) replaces this same call on full decode; whichever lands second must be measured against the other.
rules_flags: None blocking. The gate is on config (window, batch, num_kv_heads) only, with no tensor-value branching and no host sync. q_attn and attn are allocated with a fixed shape each call inside the graph, and nothing is cached across calls.

Every key is attended: causal with window_size=(-1,-1) on the same page_table and cache_seqlens. The zero half adds exactly 0 to each logit, and the discarded half is the other head's P@V, not skipped keys.

Queries stay E4M3 with identical values (copy_ and .to use the same RNE conversion), the KV cache stays FP8 and is read in place through views taken after store_cache, and the output is BF16 into the same o_norm_gate.
softmax_scale must stay explicit (sm_scale*qk_scale_factor). If it defaults to 1/sqrt(128) the result is wrong, but that is a correctness error, not a rules one; the brief already pins it.

Coverage gap, not a rules issue: in this problem the only kv_scale test is a sliding layer, so the paired descale expand(batch, S) path is never exercised by decode_layer's tests (scored shapes have kv_scale=1). It was exercised in attention_decode. The builder should copy that code verbatim.
open_questions: What is the real net overhead of the zeros + 2 pad copies + 2 un-pad copies + FA3's internal metadata prepare, against the one removed cast, at full B=16/32? Read the shape time minus kernel sum before and after. If it exceeds ~10 us, a follow-up should fuse the pad into FusedQKNorm's output or write q_pad from a tiny Triton kernel, as attention_decode's paired-heads-launch-cleanup does.
Does dist=soft (diffuse softmax) change FA3's split schedule or combine cost, compared with attention_decode's dist=coherent? The gather pattern is the same, but the combine row should be checked.

Which tests exercise page_size 64 with the paired path? batch 3 ctx 6000 full q_len 8 and batch 1 ctx 3000 full use the default page size; batch 1 ctx 3000 full is gated off. Confirm that the paired hdim-128 FP8 kernel with page_size>1 (possibly the TMA paged path) passes here, as it did in attention_decode.
Will the harvester's verdict logic mark a confirmed FA3 gain of ~1.8% on the headline as within-ci/neutral? If so, promotion should be decided on the per-shape full rows.
